source_review.notes: Reviewed the DBLP Fenwick-paper record, Fenwick's University of Auckland technical report, official AtCoder Fenwick/segtree/lazy-segtree/appendix documentation, and the author-hosted Driscoll-Sarnak-Sleator-Tarjan persistence paper. All seven final destinations returned HTTP 200. Algebra, complexity, persistence, and implementation claims remain scoped to the stated representation and assumptions.

evidence: Checked A, n, lowbit, Fenwick ownership, prefix/range, monoid/group, canonical interval, action/tag, persistence, linearization, and generation terminology.
Checked every public range is half-open and the zero-based/public to one-based/Fenwick coordinate conversion is explicit.
Checked ordinary mathematical integers are separated from concrete wrapping, checked, modular, saturating, or bounded numeric policies.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter distinguishes algebraic values, coordinates, versions, and physical storage throughout.

evidence: Recomputed initial fixture total 31, prefix [0,5)=14, and range [2,7)=21.
Recomputed Fenwick point addition at index 3, updated range [2,7)=25, cumulative sums, and lower-bound result index 4 for target 15.
Recomputed lazy range addition +3 over [1,6), total 46, range [2,7)=33, and root sum 46.
Independently constructed exercise cells [0,2,9,1,18,2,10,1,37], post-update cells [0,2,9,1,18,5,13,1,40], and ranges 20 then 23.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All interval calculations use zero-based half-open public coordinates; Fenwick cell zero is unused.

evidence: Derived the Fenwick prefix partition by repeated lowbit subtraction and ancestor updates by lowbit addition.
Derived segment query correctness from disjoint canonical coverage, source order, associativity, and identity.
Checked lazy mapping distributivity and chronological composition equations.
Independently checked affine composition (a2*a1, a2*b1+b2) against applying the older action before the newer action.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Sum-specific evidence is not treated as validation of arbitrary monoids or action families.

evidence: Reviewed empty, singleton, power-of-two, non-power-of-two, full, prefix, suffix, and invalid ranges.
Reviewed negative values, monotonicity loss, fixed-width overflow, midpoint overflow, wrong identity, padding, and noncommutative aggregation.
Reviewed noncommuting lazy actions, stale descendants, reversed composition, coordinate gaps, huge universes, allocation exhaustion, and version retention.
Reviewed corrupt sections/tags/roots, generation mismatch, publication races, reader lifetime, reclamation, restart, and denial-of-service operation mixes.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable fixture excludes empty construction, invalid inputs, generic actions, persistence, allocation failure, concurrency, serialization, corruption, and performance.

evidence: Verified every Fenwick post-update half-open interval against the plain array for 36 ranges.
Verified every lazy segment post-update half-open interval against its plain array for 36 ranges.
Verified the segment root equals the updated plain-array total after deferred range addition.
Verified exact fifteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository safe snippet runner.
invariant_checking.notes: The fixture validates finite sum representations only and stores no generic law witnesses.

evidence: Reviewed Fenwick ownership/partition and logarithmic-step arguments against positive one-based indices.
Reviewed segment canonical decomposition against half-open recursion and ordered monoid folding.
Reviewed lazy push/pull preservation against mapping, action identity, distributivity, and composition order.
Reviewed path-copying persistence against immutability of old reachable nodes while separating publication and reclamation obligations.
proof_review.notes: No proof is claimed for a concrete generic library, concurrent linearizability, reclamation scheme, durable transaction, or performance target.

evidence: Separated Fenwick group/inverse and selection preconditions from broader segment monoid capabilities.
Separated value dynamism, dynamic coordinates, implicit allocation, persistence, concurrency, and durability meanings.
The bounded Python model explicitly disclaims generic algebra, persistence, concurrency, serialization, overflow control, and production performance.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Every asymptotic claim names its controlling n, universe U, operation, or allocation model.

evidence: The standard-library model passed its exact expected output and exhaustive post-update interval comparisons.
Independent arithmetic reproduced Fenwick cells, queries, updates, lower bound, lazy totals, and affine composition.
All seven final chapter reference destinations returned HTTP 200 on the review date.
Local structure, link shape, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippet checks passed before review completion.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No AtCoder code execution, generic law property campaign, sanitizer, exhaustive operation generator, implicit/persistent implementation, concurrency model check, mapped corruption test, benchmark, or deployment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives Fenwick and segment mechanisms from distinct algebraic contracts, makes lazy composition explicit, and separates dense, implicit, persistent, concurrent, and durable variants.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed API coordinates, numeric policy, memory accounting, coordinate maps, allocation, version retention, immutable publication, reader reclamation, checked serialization, recovery, and workload-sensitive benchmarking.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet fixes the main contracts; one shared fixture contrasts point and range updates; ten examples expose boundary and systems consequences; five exercises span construction, proof, algebra design, persistence, and selection.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/author/official/bibliographic-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Fenwick, Driscoll, Sarnak, Sleator, Tarjan, AtCoder, database, streaming, geometry, numerical, concurrency, security, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither a production generic Fenwick/segment library, arbitrary monoid/action correctness, fixed-width safety, persistent allocator, concurrent linearizability, safe reclamation, mapped recovery, certification, nor deployment fitness.
